name: ExtensionInterface
summary: Lets one component export several interfaces, so that extending it neither bloats a single interface nor breaks the code of clients that do not want the extension.

reference.author: Douglas Schmidt, Michael Stal, Hans Rohnert, Frank Buschmann

roles.name: Component
roles.summary: Implements the interfaces, and is reached only through them. A client never holds this type, which is what lets the set of interfaces grow without any client being recompiled.

roles.name: RootInterface
roles.summary: The interface every extension extends, and the one that answers the question *do you also do this?* A client's whole ability to discover what a component can do is this one operation.

roles.name: ExtensionInterface
roles.summary: One coherent set of operations a component may export, extending the root. Adding another breaks nothing, which is the pattern's claim — and the cost is that a client cannot tell from the type system whether a component supports it, only by asking at run time.

roles.name: ComponentFactory
roles.summary: Creates components and hands back the root interface rather than the implementation. It is where a client's only reference to a concrete component would otherwise be.
